author: agent
text:
DESIGN DEBT, measured on this repo 2026-08-22. Two changes wanted here, recorded at the coordinate that would implement them.

THE MEASUREMENT. Of 257 knowledge entries in this repo:

  confirm  176 (68%)  14,186 words
  notes     73 (28%)  12,536 words

Two thirds of everything the workflow has produced is ATTESTATION, not knowledge. Notes carry roughly the same total words in 40% of the entries, so notes are the substantive channel and confirms are volume.

CAUSE 1 - ONE STALENESS RULE FOR TWO KINDS OF ENTRY. There are two, and they want different treatment:

  (a) claims about the code's current SHAPE - "the parse-cache comment
      names PARSE_SCHEMA_VERSION", "the margin threshold is 0.05". A body
      change can genuinely invalidate these. Staleness is correct.

  (b) constraints and reasons - "do not merge bare and via_attr, it cost
      rich and sqlalchemy their corpus floors". This is about a DECISION.
      Editing the function body does not make it false.

(b) is the valuable kind - it is the one that measurably changed an implementation this session - and it is the kind most often FALSELY staled, because it is stamped against a body hash that has nothing to do with what it asserts. One signal meaning two things, which is the pattern behind nearly every defect this project has found in itself.

CAUSE 2 - THE ONLY WAY TO CLEAR THE QUEUE IS TO WRITE PROSE. Answering means supersede or confirm, so a note that is still true demands a paragraph SAYING it is still true. Every false stale manufactures text. 176 confirms is that.

CAUSE 3 - CONFIRMS ARE ATTESTATIONS ABOUT ATTESTATIONS AND THEY STALE TOO. A confirm on X stales when X's body moves, demanding a confirm on the confirm. Self-perpetuating by construction; the seven identical confirms on memway.__init__ are the specimen.

WANTED, CHEAP FIRST: `confirm` should be a RE-STAMP, not an append. "Somebody checked this at hash H" is a stamp, not prose - appending 80 words to say it is what generates the volume. A new entry only when the author actually has something to say. On these numbers that is 176 -> roughly 30.

WANTED, STRUCTURAL: let an entry declare its kind. A constraint does not stale on a body edit; it wants review when the thing it constrains is REMOVED, or never automatically at all. Then staleness means "this might now be wrong" rather than "this file moved".

NOT YET BUILT. Recorded here rather than in CLAUDE.md because it is a fact about how this module's stamping behaves, not a method lesson - and because whoever opens MetaStore.add or for_display next should see it before they touch either.

author: agent
text:
BUILT in 0.61.0, superseding the design-debt entry below. Both halves of what that note asked for, plus a cause it did not know about.

SHIPPED: MetaStore.reaffirm, and the affirm door on CLI and MCP. An affirmation is now a STAMP - it re-dates the claims already in a channel and writes no prose. It takes no position in the reading order (for_display skips it), because supersession is positional and a textless entry taking a slot would mark the very note it vouches for as superseded history. It refuses on an empty channel: the first attestation must say something or the feature is a mute button, and that refusal is the whole safety of it.

NOT SHIPPED, and still wanted: the entry KIND. A constraint ('do not merge bare and via_attr') is about a decision and should not stale when a body is reformatted; a claim about current shape should. One staleness rule still serves both.

THE CAUSE THAT NOTE MISSED, found by following the ceremony it was written during. Comment rot hashed comments[i].text, which is truncated to 200 characters for DISPLAY. So rot could see only the first 200 characters of a docstring - 39% of this map's 785 commented entities carry a comment at that cut. Consequences ran both ways and the quiet one is worse: a docstring CORRECTED past the cut does not clear the flag, so the only exit is to write a confirm for a docstring you actually fixed; and a typo fix INSIDE the cut clears rot on a docstring that is still wrong. Detection now hashes the full text (indexer._ctext_hash) while display stays bounded. This was not a discipline problem at all - it was a display bound doing a detector's job, which is the same one-value-two-meanings shape as via_attr, of literal_recv, and of staleness itself.
replaces: the design-debt note said NOT YET BUILT; the cheap half is now built, and the ceremony that followed found a second, unrelated cause of the same confirm volume
